title: Difference Quotient of a Shifted Reciprocal
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x)=1/(x+1), simplify the difference quotient (f(x+h)-f(x))/h, h != 0.

steps.title: Write the Two Values
steps.explanation: Replacing x by x+h shifts the denominator from x+1 to x+1+h.
steps.why: The increment h enters the linear denominator directly.

steps.title: Subtract Over a Common Denominator
steps.explanation: Cross-combining the fractions makes the numerator collapse to -h.

steps.title: Divide by h and Cancel
steps.explanation: Canceling h (allowed since h != 0) produces the simplified quotient.
steps.why: The leftover factor h in the numerator is designed to cancel the outer division.
